input.brief: Bellis Australia: industrial mechanical insulation distributor, metal fabricator and installer serving LNG, power, mining, marine and defence plants

direction.name: Dressed as something else
direction.idea: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.
direction.composition: Depends on the borrowed category, so decide it explicitly and write it in your notes. Fashion drop: one shouted condensed headline across the full width, a single cropped image under it, then product facts as a blunt list. Watch or perfume: a centred object on a dark field, a small serif name, very few words, long vertical pauses. Poster or zine: flat colour blocks, heavy type, tilted cut-out images. Museum: one item per screen on a plinth-like band of colour with a short label beside it. Whichever you choose, the page structure stays simple (four to six sections) and every section uses the borrowed manners, including pricing and the footer.
direction.typography: The borrowed category's type, fully committed: condensed and loud, or refined and small. No halfway.
direction.colour: The borrowed category's palette, which will be unlike the subject's sector norm. That mismatch is intended.
direction.imagery: Photograph the subject the way the borrowed category would be photographed. With the dealt set, choose images for attitude, not literal relevance, and crop them hard.
direction.richness: Attitude. The page has a recognisable voice from another world, applied to a subject nobody expected it for.
direction.pitfalls: Name the borrowed category in one word before you start, or the result is merely loud. The content must still be clear: what it is, what it costs, how to get it. Avoid borrowing from 'tech startup', which is the default you are escaping.

hero.name: Single specimen with name list
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a museum plinth. A calm light ground with roughly 70% left empty. The wordmark is set large for a logo, about 28% of the viewport wide (clamp(64px, 6vw, 92px), heavy serif or grotesk), top-left on a 56px margin; one sentence of description at 15px sits top-right on the same margin, its first line aligned to the top of the wordmark. Dead centre stands one specimen: a flat tile in a palette colour, 400px wide and 460px tall (columns 5-8) with a 16px radius, holding a single cut-out item at about 80% of the tile height, object-fit: contain. Left of the tile, in columns 2-4, a vertical list of item names is right-aligned towards it: the selected name in full ink at 20px, the names above and below stepping down in size and opacity (18, 16, 14px; 60, 35, 15%). Choosing a name swaps the item and the tile colour. Below the tile, centred: the item's one-line fact at 14px, then the single action, a filled rectangle 240px wide. Three text links sit bottom-left at 14px.
hero.mobile: The wordmark sits top-left at 11vw with the description sentence beneath it at 15px. The tile takes the full width inside 20px margins at 4:5, starting at 30% of the height. The name list becomes one horizontal row under the tile that scrolls sideways with scroll-snap, the selected name centred in full ink at 18px. The action sits full width at the bottom of the screen; the links move to the footer.
hero.headline: The name itself as an oversized wordmark, up to 10 characters on one line; there is no separate statement.

type.note: Road-sign condensed type with squared curves, bold but not compressed into a wall, with its normal-width sibling for text. Suits logistics, motorsport, hardware and directories with many short titles.

palette.name: Grey, mint, orange
palette.note: Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange in turn. Photographs inside a flooded section are shown in black-and-white, and mint is also the button colour on white and black.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Comparison set as text
sections.blueprint: A comparison table with no lines and no tick marks. A CSS grid: capability names in columns 1–5 of 12 at 22–24px medium, then three answer columns of equal width (plans, methods, or this against the usual way). Every cell answers in words at 17px: 'Yes, unlimited', 'Up to five', 'Not yet', never a symbol. Seven to ten rows, each 64–72px tall, with every other row on a ground one tone darker so the eye tracks across; rows touch. The column that matters is one filled block in the accent or ink colour running the full height of the table behind its cells and rising 24px above the first row, with its text reversed. Column names sit in the top row at 17px bold. The heading, two to four words at 40–48px, hangs top-left above column 1 with 48px beneath.
sections.mobile: The table turns on its side: one block per capability. The name at 20px bold, then three lines beneath, each giving a column name and its answer at 16px; the featured column's line is set on the filled colour at full width. Blocks alternate the two ground tones.

sections.name: Output slips along the edge
sections.blueprint: For subjects whose result is a piece of text or paper: a receipt, a note, a ticket, a written line. A full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 96svh, sets the scene. In the upper centre, left-aligned in a column starting at 18% of the width, two short paragraphs in paper colour at 28–32px, the first opening with the heading's two to four words; a neutral scrim sits behind that column only. Along the bottom, six paper-coloured slips stand side by side across the full width with 12px gaps, each a filled rectangle of a different height (between 26 and 44svh), their lower ends cut off by the section's bottom edge. Two or three of the slips, not all, are tilted by 1–2 degrees. Each slip carries a sample of real output in the text face at 15px: a bold first line, a divider made of typed characters, then four to eight lines.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100svh. The paragraphs sit in the top third at 22px. Only three slips show, each 30vw wide, standing along the bottom at different heights, and the row scrolls sideways to reveal the rest. Slip text stays at 14px; do not scale it down.

sections.name: Many into one
sections.blueprint: A diagram drawn with one repeated shape instead of arrows. The heading (two to four words on two lines at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px)) and a short paragraph at 17px sit in columns 1–4. Beneath, a wide inline SVG spans columns 1–12 at about 4.5:1. It is built from 120–160 small filled squares (or the page's own motif), each 10–14px. In the left third they are scattered loosely in two pale tones. In the middle third they are pulled into a tight horizontal ribbon three squares high. In the right third they fan out again into neat, evenly spaced rows in the accent colour. The eye reads disorder, compression, order, from left to right. Under the diagram, three text columns aligned to its thirds: a bold one-word name at 20px and two lines at 16px each; the words carry the sequence ('Gather', 'Reduce', 'Release'). No connecting marks.
sections.mobile: The diagram turns to run top to bottom: a 3:4 SVG with the scatter at the top, the ribbon as a vertical band in the middle and the ordered rows at the bottom. The three names and their text sit to its right in a 38vw column, each level with its zone.

sections.name: The printed guest list
sections.blueprint: Names are printed on a card, the way a programme lists its patrons or an invitation its hosts. On a contrasting flat ground, a paper-coloured panel about 56% of the viewport wide with 5:7 proportions sits centred and rotated by one or two degrees; the section is shorter than the card and clips it with `overflow: hidden`, so the card is cut by the bottom edge rather than framed whole. Inside, 56px padding. At the top, a centred heading of two to four words at 28px. Below it the names run as centred lines at 20–22px with leading 1.7, several names to a line, separated by middots with a non-breaking space either side. One photograph may be tipped in between the heading and the names: 16:9, the full inner width, square corners. The card is a plain filled shape with no outline.
sections.mobile: The card becomes 92% of the screen wide, keeps a one-degree tilt and is still cut off by the section's bottom edge. Heading at 22px, names at 17px with two names to a line. Padding drops to 28px, and the tipped-in photograph keeps the full inner width.

sections.name: Total and its receipt
sections.blueprint: A total at giant size, and beside it the slip that adds up to it. Left, columns 1–6: at the top the heading, two to five words at 40–44px, with a two-line note at 16px; at the bottom-left, anchored to the section's lower edge, the total at clamp(160px, 18vw, 300px) with leading 0.8, and one caption line at 17px under it. The space between heading and total is left empty. Right, columns 8–11: a paper-coloured slip 380–440px wide on the section's contrasting ground, top-aligned with the heading, its bottom edge a zigzag made with clip-path. The slip lists eight to fourteen rows in the text face at 15–16px with tabular numerals, grouped under bold group names; each row has a description on the left, a right-aligned value, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The last row is inverted on a solid ink bar and repeats the total. The slip's values must truly sum to the figure.
sections.mobile: Heading and note come first. The total follows at 40vw, flush left, with its caption. The slip comes last at full width minus 16px margins with its zigzag edge, rows at 15px, and the inverted total row closing it.

sections.name: Object riding down the schedule
sections.blueprint: A schedule of dated events (races, concerts, tastings, departures) with the subject's own object travelling down it. On a dark flat ground, on the page's own margins, the heading is one centred line of condensed capitals at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px), split into its two words with a gap between them, and in the gap stands a cut-out photograph of the object seen from above or in profile, about 320px wide (22% of the width) and up to 64% of the viewport tall. Below come full-width rows 84px tall, each a two-part grid: the event's name at 26px in condensed capitals on the left with a one-line note at 16px in the soft ink under it, and the date and place right-aligned at 16px on the note's baseline. Rows alternate between the ground and a tone one step lighter instead of rules. As the page scrolls, the object leaves the heading and moves down the centre line over the rows (`position: sticky` in a centred column that spans the list, `pointer-events: none`), where it covers only the empty middle of each row and marks how far the reader has come. The row for the next event takes the accent colour across its whole band, with its name and date in the accent's ink. About ten rows fit on one screen; the list ends 120px under the last row.
sections.mobile: Rows stack at full width on 20px margins: the name at 22px on up to two lines, the note at 16px, the date under the note. The object shrinks to 40% of the width and stays in the heading; it does not travel, because on a phone it would cover the rows. The accent band stays on the next event.

sections.name: Clip-out coupon form
sections.blueprint: The form is a coupon to cut out. One filled card in a strong flat colour, about 2.2:1, spans columns 2–11 with a 14px radius, with 120px of ground above and below. Semicircular notches 28px across are cut into its top and bottom edges at the 46% mark with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`, and a vertical row of round dots (a dotted `border-left` 5px thick in the ground colour) joins the two notches as the perforation. Left of the perforation, with 48px padding: a two-line heading of three to five words at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px) in heavy capitals at the top, and one sentence at 16px at the bottom. Right of it: four inputs stacked with 10px gaps, each a filled block 52px tall in a lighter tone of the card with its placeholder at 16px, then a full-width solid submit bar 56px tall in the darkest ink. Inputs keep visually hidden `label` elements.
sections.mobile: The card turns upright and spans the width with 12px margins. The perforation becomes horizontal: notches on the left and right edges, dots across. Heading and sentence sit above it; the four inputs and the submit bar sit below, each 54px tall.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Contact as the headline
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall. Top row, 40px from the edge: two or three short notes at 15px in columns 1–7 (address, hours, a one-line description) and a back-to-top text link at the right margin. Then a tall empty gap. In the lower half, the way to get in touch is the display line: the telephone number or the email address itself, set at 8–9vw, flush left, hard against the margin, as one link. An email address may break once, before the @, giving two lines. Size it with `clamp()` so the longest line fills at least 80% of the width. Under it, one row of small text at 14px spread across three positions: links at the left, credits in the centre, city and year at the right. The wordmark appears only small, in the top row.
sections.mobile: Notes stack at the top at 15px. The contact line sits in the lower half at 12vw; a telephone number stays on one line, an email breaks before the @ and is sized so each half fits the width. The meta row becomes three stacked lines at 13px.

references.name: CoffeeTech®
references.idea: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with nothing but type. A centred three-line headline, one word per line, in Inter Medium at about 15vw with tight tracking; the first line starts a third of the way down and the last runs to within 35px of the bottom edge, its widest word spanning roughly 70% of the width. Cream letters; no subhead, no media, no hero button. Navigation is one quiet row: logo with a terracotta mark at left, four text links centred, then a filled terracotta 'Products' button with a grid icon, an outlined contact button and a language dropdown at right. The top third stays empty.
references.type: Inter throughout at weight 500. Display lines at 216px with -0.07em tracking and leading near 0.95 against 14px body, a jump of about 15 times. Secondary headlines near 10vw, intro paragraph around 26px. Section labels are tiny and wrapped in square brackets.
references.colour: #0d0e13 #e5e2dd #f3ece2 #c8603d #262629 — Blue-black and warm putty-grey sections alternate; cream type on dark, near-black on light. Terracotta appears only on the logo mark and the primary button.
references.imagery: Studio shots of roasters: a black machine barely lit against black after the hero, then white and black machines as cut-outs on pale-grey tiles. One warm founder portrait with a signature overlapping its edge; macro bean photos in small-radius cards.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 70px. A centred type poster on top, then an offset two-column intro, then a product grid pushed into the right two-thirds with its bracketed label alone in the left third. Oversized left-flush headlines open and close the lower page.

sections.description: Warm putty-grey band entered through a hairline. A portrait about 290px wide with 8px corners sits in the left third; a scrawled signature overlaps its bottom-right corner and spills onto the background. A seven-line paragraph at about 26px, medium weight, roughly 510px wide, begins at the horizontal midpoint, followed by a small underlined text link. No heading; the right quarter and the gap between the two elements stay empty.

A headline at roughly 10vw is flush to the left edge and clipped by the right, like a slow marquee. Below, a tiny bracketed label sits alone in the left third; the right two-thirds hold a two-column grid of pale-grey tiles about 400px wide with a small radius, each with a centred machine cut-out, the model name beneath and a tiny outlined pill for its category. The grid closes with a 64px underlined 'see all' text link with an arrow.

Back to blue-black. A cream contact headline at about 10vw sits hard against the left edge, far larger than anything near it. Underneath, the terracotta logo mark is enlarged to about 140px at left; four narrow link columns in small grey text run from 28% to 85% of the width; a pill-shaped back-to-top button sits at far right, with a thin legal row at the bottom.

steal: Let a three-word headline at about 15vw be the entire first viewport and withhold the product until the first scroll.
Photograph a dark product on a background matching the page colour so it appears to emerge from the page rather than sit in a box.
Overlap a handwritten signature onto the corner of a portrait so an about block feels signed rather than laid out.
references.media: The fold is type only; one scroll later a full-bleed low-key photograph of the roaster on matching black covers 76% of the screen, so the object floats out of the dark as the second beat of the hero. Below: a portrait with a signature over its edge, product renders contained on tinted tiles in a 2x2 grid, three 4:5 macro ingredient cards with the label docked bottom-left, and a blog slider; 25 images, no video, about 12.5px corners on card media.
references.motion: No entrance at all: the 400ms frame already matches the settled one. No smooth scroll, pins or sticky elements; a model scale-in keyframe over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.36,.18,0,.99) with a 1.5s glow grows the roaster into place, link underlines wipe in by clip-path over 2.5s, overlay panels slide in over 0.8s, and the most common duration is 0.3s.

references.name: Locker Land
references.idea: A dry B2B parcel-locker pitch dressed as a fairground of die-cut stickers, where the main navigation is a fan of five tilted illustrated cards.
references.hero: Post-red field overlaid with a faint lighter-red square grid. Small white brand lock-up top-left; a white pill button with a hard dark-red offset shadow top-right. Top-centre, a two-line sticker-style logo (cream letters, thick cream outline, small locker drawing) about 20% of viewport width. Beneath it a two-line centred white sentence at 18px; no larger headline. The lower half is a fan of five portrait cards with thick coloured frames and rounded corners: centre card upright, neighbours rotated about 8 degrees, the outer pair about 18 degrees and cropped by the viewport edges, each with a label tab overlapping its bottom edge. A two-line caption sits centred below.
references.type: apDisplay, a brand grotesque, is the only family: weight 500, sentence case, slightly tight. Body 16-18px; section headings in dark red reach about 5.9vw. The hero has no typographic headline, the sticker logo plays that role. Labels inside sticker tabs go bold.
references.colour: #dc1928 #fdf3db #952625 #e0a912 #5b7a94 #d46831 — Post red and cream alternate as full section fields; mustard, slate blue, burnt orange and maroon are reserved for card frames and badges. Warm, flat, no gradients.
references.imagery: Flat vector drawings (parcel, locker, hand holding a card) with thick cream die-cut outlines and hard offset shadows, plus candid photos of people at lockers placed inside arch-shaped cut-outs and wide rounded video tiles.
references.layout: Every section is a centre-stacked composition on a full-width colour field, with a pill-shaped sticky sub-nav top-centre after the hero. Sections are separated by ornament rather than whitespace: a red and cream checkerboard strip, a scalloped awning edge. Cards come in tilted rows of three or five.

sections.description: On red beneath a checkerboard strip, a dark-red pill with a dotted inner border holds the heading. Three statistics are scattered as tilted stickers instead of a row: a mustard circle, a maroon starburst seal with a cursor-arrow sticker overlapping it, and a slate-blue tag shape, each with a small parcel or locker illustration tucked onto a corner. Figures are large; captions are tiny and centred inside each shape.

On cream, the heading sits in a white rounded box with dark-red outline and offset shadow, hanging directly under the sticky nav. Below, three equal portrait cards in mustard, slate blue and orange, each with a dark-red border and hard offset shadow, containing an arch-shaped photo cut-out of people, a tilted name-tag sticker, a starburst date badge, two centred lines of copy and a small white pill button.

A centred locker illustration with icon stickers orbiting it, a centred heading and two-line intro, then a full-width two-by-two mosaic of video stills with no gaps and rounded outer corners. Each tile carries one large white rounded chip with a bold red word, placed low and off-centre. A hand-drawn orange arrow sticker overlaps the mosaic's top-left corner, pointing in.

Five stacked white pill-shaped rows in a centred column about 65% of the page wide, each with dark-red outline, hard offset shadow, question at left and chevron at right. A checkerboard strip then returns the page to red, where an oversized version of the sticker logo sits centred with a one-line copyright beneath.

steal: Turn the primary navigation into a fan of tilted illustrated cards in the hero, centre card upright and the outer ones rotated and cropped by the viewport edges.
Give every element the same die-cut sticker treatment (thick cream outline plus a hard, unblurred offset shadow in a darker shade of the background) so buttons, cards and badges read as one family.
Present statistics as differently shaped badges (circle, starburst, tag) scattered at angles rather than as three equal columns.

references.name: poetry camera
references.idea: A camera that prints poems is sold through its own output: copy arrives as thermal-paper slips, and a soft-focus bitmap wordmark lies over handheld footage.
references.hero: Full-bleed handheld video of two hands holding the white-and-red camera against out-of-focus blossom. The product name is centred over it in two lines of white lowercase bitmap lettering about 10vw tall, deliberately blurred so the pixels bloom into soft blobs; the block spans 70% of the width, from 25% to 70% of the height, directly on top of the camera. One text link sits top-left and two social icons top-right, all white. A yellow pill button about 165px wide with black lowercase text is centred near the bottom edge and stays fixed for the whole page. No tagline and no scrim.
references.type: BitMatrix A2, a dot-matrix face, blurred at 10vw for the wordmark and sharp at 12px on the paper slips; Exposure, a soft serif, in white lowercase near 32px for statements and about 10vw for the closing quote; DM Sans for links and button.
references.colour: #b7a590 #7a6f3e #f9fdf9 #ffde5b #c92a2a #1a1a1a — Colour comes from the footage: blossom pinks, moss greens, the camera's red base. White type and off-white paper slips sit over it; one yellow button repeats on every screen. The last screen turns plain white.
references.imagery: Soft, shallow-focus handheld video fills each screen: the camera outdoors, on a workbench, prototypes on a desk. Over it sit scanned-looking thermal slips with mono text and dithered halftone portraits, slightly rotated and overlapping.
references.layout: Each section is one full-height video with a block of large white serif text in a central column about 45% wide, left-aligned, and a row of paper slips rising from the bottom edge. The same yellow button floats bottom-centre throughout. The page ends on a type-only white screen.

sections.description: Full-bleed video of the camera hanging among blossom. Two short paragraphs of white lowercase serif near 32px sit in the upper centre, left-aligned in a column starting 18% in. Along the bottom, six off-white paper slips of differing heights stand side by side across the full width, each tilted a degree or two, each headed by a lowercase mono label and a typed divider of dashes or crosses, then a short poem in mono. The bottom edge crops them.

Same structure over a different clip. Three tall receipt-like slips fan out beneath a three-line serif statement, each tilted differently and overlapping slightly. A slip carries a name between rows of asterisks, a one-line role, a typed rule, a circular dithered black-and-white portrait, then the quote in 12px mono. The slips run off the bottom of the screen.

Plain off-white screen with no image. A quotation is set in black lowercase serif at about 10vw with the words of each line spread to the full width: one hard left, one centred, one hard right. Two lines are visible with 150px between them, and the attribution is spaced the same way. Beneath, four small sans links centred in a row, then the yellow button.

steal: Blur a bitmap wordmark until the pixels bloom, turning a hard retro face into something soft enough to sit on video without a scrim.
Present feature copy and testimonials as the product's own printed artefact (tilted receipt slips with typed dividers and dithered portraits) rather than cards.
Close on a type-only screen with a quote spread word by word across the full width, as a change of tempo after continuous video.
